summary: Grade 8 of McGraw Hill's StudySync Core ELA: six thematic units on mystery, identity, risk, persuasion, crisis and speculative fiction, each with an essential question and a genre focus. Texts range from Poe, Jackson and Anne Frank to speeches by Lincoln, Churchill and Reagan; each unit ends in an Extended Writing or Oral Project (narrative, argument, informative, argument, advocacy speech, research).

toc.label: Unit 1
toc.title: Everyone Loves a Mystery
toc.covers: Essential question "What attracts us to the mysterious?"; genre focus fiction, with suspense stories, horror classics and true mysteries; Extended Writing Project is a suspenseful narrative in which fear comes from an unlikely source; grammar: basic spelling rules I, dashes, commas after transitions.

notes: ISBNs on the school list include the Unit 2 ("Past and Present", 9781944695866) and Unit 3 ("No Risk, No Reward", 9781944695873) Reading & Writing Companions, per AbeBooks; the other two ISBNs (9781949739251, 9781949739329) are 2021 BookheadEd printings, likely other unit volumes or teacher materials (not verified). Each unit is printed as its own consumable Reading & Writing Companion volume (Unit 1 to Unit 6, per the retailer listings); the digital platform carries further texts, Blasts, StudySyncTV episodes and English Language Learner resources (general). Every unit ends in an Extended Writing Project (one unit per grade uses an Extended Oral Project instead) taught through Plan, Draft, Revise, Edit and Publish steps (page). Texts listed here are the unit selections named in the McGraw Hill Grade Level Overview; several are excerpts from full-length books, and some (marked Independent Read in the program) are read without full lesson support. The Overview credits the Phineas Gage book to W. W. Jacobs in error; its author is John Fleischman (general).
